title: Introduce content-addressable stamped layer cache and adaptive priming for monorepo builds
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem:
Our monorepo build latency for incremental PRs has regressed due to layer churn, non-deterministic Dockerfile ordering, and cache misses from machine-local caches. CI queue time is high for cross-language targets (Go services, Node packages, Python tools).

Goal:
- Implement a content-addressable stamped layer cache (CAS-style) for BuildKit that produces stable cache keys across runners and reduces warm-up misses.
- Add an adaptive cache-priming job that materializes hot build artifacts into the remote cache after merge to main.
- Standardize small, deterministic Docker layer stamps for language toolchain installs so identical inputs map to the same cache entries.
- Upgrade Node 18->20 and Go 1.20->1.22 in build images and ensure lints/tooling remain compatible.

Acceptance criteria:
- Median cold-start build for small packages drops from ~120s to <=60s, and warm incremental builds for common PRs drop from ~40s to <=15s (measured in CI run_time).
- CI cache hit rate for targeted job group increases by >=40% within 2 weeks of rollout.
- No regression in linting or tests; external flaky tests decreased or documented for follow-ups.
- Rollback plan defined and exercised in one trial deployment.

Implementation notes & plan:
1) Proof of concept (1 sprint)
   - Add BuildKit remote cache backed by S3 with content-addressable keys (stamp = sha256 of Dockerfile fragment + build args + toolchain lockfile).
   - Instrument cache metrics (hit/miss, retrieval latency) and expose to Grafana.
   - Validate correctness with three representative packages: web-frontend, auth-service, evals-tooling.

2) Stabilize + priming (1 sprint)
   - Add nightly cache-priming job that rebuilds release artifacts and pushes to remote cache.
   - Implement adaptive priming: detect top-20 changed targets from recent merged PRs and prime those.

3) Toolchain upgrades and lint gating (0.5 sprint)
   - Bake Node 20 and Go 1.22 into new minimal builder images; run full CI matrix to find regressions.
   - Update ESLint/TS rules and Go linters; gate PRs with faster pre-submit lint-only checks using local cache.

4) Rollout (0.5 sprint)
   - Run pilot with 2 squads, monitor cache hit rate and CI duration.
   - Gradually flip primary CI jobs to use remote CAS.

Risks and mitigations:
- Cache poisoning due to non-deterministic Dockerfiles: mitigate by normalizing Dockerfile fragments and adding a stamp generation test in CI.
- Increased S3 costs for remote cache: limit TTLs and configure compression; monitor cost dashboard.
- Toolchain regressions: keep legacy builder images available and add quick rollback toggle in CI config.

Artifacts and links:
- Confluence PRD: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/CI+CAS+Design (design/ci-cas.md)
- Draft implementation RFC: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1XYZci-cas-draft
- Pilot PR (build infra): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/412
- Cache dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ci-cache/remote-cache-overview
- Benchmark results (initial POC): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1poC-cache-bench

Migration & rollback plan:
- Feature flag in CI job templates to switch between local and remote cache. Initial pilot sets flag for pilot repos only.
- If hit rate or failure rate worsens beyond threshold (2x failures or >=10% increase in median build time), flip flag off and roll back builder image to previous base.

Notes for reviewers:
- We will need infra S3 bucket policy and lifecycle rules (requesting costs/ops from cloud team).
- Security review: no secrets will be stored in cache keys; stamp generation must exclude environment-specific values.
